name: Matix media
note: Every film is generated procedurally from math (Python + pycairo + C, encoded with x264). Muted H.264 MP4.

gallery.title: Mandelbrot deep zoom
gallery.sub: Zoom 640 million times into z → z² + c — the edge never runs out of new shapes

gallery.title: Fourier epicycles
gallery.sub: Any drawing is just circles spinning on circles

gallery.title: Julia sets in motion
gallery.sub: Slide c around the Mandelbrot set and the Julia set of z² + c melts and re-forms

gallery.title: The Lorenz attractor
gallery.sub: Three simple equations for weather — and the butterfly of chaos appears

gallery.title: The golden angle
gallery.sub: Turn 137.5° between seeds and a sunflower appears — Fibonacci spirals for free

gallery.title: The chaos game
gallery.sub: Jump halfway to a random corner, again and again — order appears out of randomness

gallery.title: Chaos: the double pendulum
gallery.sub: Six pendulums start 0.0001 rad apart — within seconds they disagree completely

gallery.title: Times tables on a circle
gallery.sub: Join n to k·n (mod 200): k = 2 makes a cardioid, then it keeps morphing

gallery.title: Newton's fractal
gallery.sub: Colour every start point by the root of z³ − 1 that Newton's method lands on

gallery.title: The Galton board
gallery.sub: Each ball flips left or right 14 times — together they draw the bell curve

gallery.title: Lissajous table
gallery.sub: x = sin(a·t), y = sin(b·t) — every pair of frequencies makes its own curve

gallery.title: The Ulam spiral
gallery.sub: Write 1, 2, 3… in a square spiral and light up the primes — diagonals appear

gallery.title: Sine & cosine
gallery.sub: Walk round the unit circle — your height draws the sine wave

gallery.title: Conway's Game of Life
gallery.sub: Two rules — born with 3 neighbours, survive with 2 or 3 — and gliders start to fly

gallery.title: A 4-D hypercube
gallery.sub: A tesseract turning through the fourth dimension, projected down to your screen

gallery.title: Finding π with random darts
gallery.sub: Fraction of darts inside the quarter circle × 4  →  π

gallery.title: Pythagoras, proved by moving
gallery.sub: Same big square, same 4 triangles — so the leftover areas must match

gallery.title: Fractal curves
gallery.sub: Koch snowflake: infinite edge, finite area. Hilbert curve: a line that fills a square

gallery.title: One-line universes
gallery.sub: Each row follows a tiny rule from the row above — Rule 30, Rule 90, Rule 110
